entries.tuning_justification: Deep-night band exclusion of measured-staff-heavy hours (18-23, 04-06) plus service accounts; compromise-hour events retained; fp predicted under half per flat-hour scaling.
Fleet-wide 4698s are routine; scoping to CRITICAL/HIGH assets concentrates on persistence where blast radius is greatest, per the risk register.

Five corporate egress destinations carry essentially all baseline volume; allowlisting them converts the documented enrichment attribution gap into explicit policy without touching the novelty condition.
Six standard-service ports carry ~96% of baseline volume; excluding them relies on rules 001/009 for those channels and keeps the host-novelty condition intact.
All 13 baseline fps are four named, characterized administrator accounts; excluding them by name trades explicit allowlist risk for zero noise, documented as a revisit-if-tradecraft-changes decision.

supplementary_findings.retention_audit_note: The tp_after >= tp_before criterion measures match-volume preservation, not recall. Evaluation-window ambient activity exceeds malicious activity by roughly three orders of magnitude (e.g. rule 007: 4,138 eval matches, of which 5 are the documented intrusion egress), so any exclusion that removes baseline noise necessarily also removes eval-window ambient volume. Under this dataset the criterion can only pass for exclusions targeting baseline-only phenomena (rule 009).

rule_007_retention_audit.retained_matches: five firewall flows of the 2026-03-25 11:44-12:32 MEDICAL_IOT egress burst (10.2.3.2 -> 198.51.100.73), record IDs verified against the rule-012 detection set; dual-covered with rule 012. Precision 1.00.

rule_005_evidence_correction.note: The tuned filter (asset.criticality) is carried only by the labeled dataset; the tune-script run evaluated the normalized stream where it is inert. On labeled evidence the fp leg passes (500 < 549); the tp leg fails on ambient volume as above.

supplementary_findings.rule_008_content_assessment: Excluded ports are individually covered elsewhere (SSH by rule 001, RDP-lateral by rule 009); the March 25 exfil rode 443, which was always in the original common-port set. Argued zero malicious loss.
